title: Tidy the whole room
brief:
Beepers are scattered all over the room. Pick up every one of them. Where Karel finishes does not matter.

Tested on two rooms of different sizes. In the second room, one square has two beepers on it.

This task uses everything from weeks 2 and 3: helper functions, while loops and if. Plan first: how do you clean one row? How do you get to the next row? When do you stop?

vocabulary.gloss: True if there is no wall on Karel's left side
decide the steps in words before you write code
a line that does nothing. It keeps a function valid while it is still empty — replace it with real commands

worlds.name: Bigger room, one square with two beepers

hints: clean_square() should be a while loop, not an if: while beepers_present(): pick_beeper(). clean_row() cleans the square Karel is on, then repeats 'move, clean' while front_is_clear().

After a row, Karel is at the east wall facing east. Go back: turn_around(), walk while front_is_clear(), turn_around() again. Now Karel is at the west wall facing east. Is there a row above? left_is_clear() tells you.
main(): clean_row(), go back. Then while left_is_clear(): turn_left(), move(), turn_right(), clean_row(), go back. Write 'go back' as its own helper function.
